cases.title: Stable Restorative Sleep (Stage N2)
cases.description: Healthy adult sleep characterized by natural brainwave bursts (sleep spindles and K-complexes) that protect the brain from waking up and help lock in memory.

cases.title: Deep Slow-Wave Sleep (Stage N3)
cases.description: The deepest, most physically restorative sleep stage marked by synchronized delta waves, responsible for muscle repair, immune rebuilding, and brain detoxification.

cases.title: Fragmented Sleep & Night Arousals (WASO)
cases.description: Frequent night awakenings and restless light sleep after initial sleep onset, showing persistent wakefulness brain patterns that disrupt restful sleep cycles.

cases.title: Active Dream State (Stage REM)
cases.description: Vivid dreaming sleep featuring rapid eye movements, low-voltage active brain signals, and complete muscle relaxation to process daily emotions and ideas.

cases.title: Acute Cognitive Stress (Mental Math)
cases.description: Sharp increase in mental tension recorded during speed arithmetic, displaying sudden frontal brainwave suppression and fast beta stress bursts.

cases.title: Relaxed Baseline Rest (Eyes Closed)
cases.description: Calm resting condition with steady 10 Hz alpha brain rhythms, showing an unburdened, relaxed neural baseline free from acute tension or strain.

cases.title: Cognitive Conflict & Exam Stress
cases.description: Mental strain and friction triggered during timed decision-making tests, capturing strong frontal-central neural indicators of student workload stress.

cases.title: Acute State Anxiety & Emotional Arousal
cases.description: Heightened emotional tension and nervous arousal during psychological stimulation, showing rapid desynchronized prefrontal brainwave patterns.

cases.title: Peaceful Pre-Test Baseline
cases.description: Smooth, balanced background brainwaves recorded before stimulation, confirming a peaceful state without signs of panic, agitation, or anxious distress.

cases.title: Pre-Apnea Early Warning Window
cases.description: Early warning brainwave and breathing indicators captured 90 seconds prior to airway obstruction, detecting subtle oxygen and autonomic changes before collapse.

guidelines.document_title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Pharmacologic & Behavioral Treatment of Chronic Insomnia in Adults
guidelines.section_title: Management of Prolonged Sleep Latency and Nocturnal Arousal
guidelines.citation_reference: Sateia et al., Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 13(2):307-349 (2017/2021)
guidelines.chunk_content: When persistent nocturnal wakefulness (elevated WASO >30 minutes or prolonged sleep latency) is observed, implement stimulus control therapy: advise the individual not to remain in bed tossing for extended periods. Maintain dark, quiet ambient conditions (temp 18-20°C). Avoid screen exposure and blue light emittance which suppresses melatonin production. Screen for psychophysiological insomnia and underlying nocturnal triggers.

guidelines.document_title: AASM Manual for the Scoring of Sleep and Associated Events: Rules, Terminology and Technical Specifications
guidelines.section_title: Stage N1 Criteria & Environmental Sleep Architecture Preservation
guidelines.citation_reference: Berry et al., American Academy of Sleep Medicine Manual v2.6 (2020)
guidelines.chunk_content: Stage N1 represents the vulnerable sleep-wake transition with elevated sensory arousal thresholds. Disproportionately elevated N1 percentage (>10-12% of total sleep time) is a primary hallmark of sleep fragmentation, frequent micro-arousals, or periodic limb movements. Ensure acoustic attenuation and evaluate for occult sleep-disordered breathing if N1 persists without rapid consolidation into N2.

guidelines.document_title: Consensus Conference on Sleep Health and Adult Restorative Architecture
guidelines.section_title: Stage N2 Sleep Spindle Density & Cortical Stabilization
guidelines.chunk_content: Stage N2 accounts for 45-55% of normal adult sleep architecture, characterized by synchronous 12-14 Hz sleep spindles and biphasic K-complexes that shield the cortex against intrusive sensory arousal. Preserve uninterrupted nocturnal duration to ensure memory consolidation and cognitive recovery. Avoid pharmacological agents that suppress natural sleep spindle rhythmicity.

guidelines.document_title: AASM Practice Guidelines: Restorative Sleep Homeostasis & Slow-Wave Deficiency
guidelines.section_title: Stage N3 Slow-Wave Deep Sleep Clinical Significance
guidelines.citation_reference: Kapur et al., J Clin Sleep Med, 13(3):479-504 (2019/2021)
guidelines.chunk_content: Stage N3 (Slow-Wave Deep Sleep) is essential for physical repair, glymphatic brain clearance, and growth hormone secretion. Severe reduction of N3 (<10-15% of TST) correlates with daytime fatigue, cognitive slowing, and impaired immune response. Minimize late evening alcohol, sedatives, and caffeine intake which prematurely truncate slow-wave synchronization. Maintain rigorous circadian consistency.

guidelines.document_title: Practice Parameters for the Evaluation and Treatment of REM Parasomnias and Disorders
guidelines.section_title: REM Sleep Architecture, Motor Atonia and Safety
guidelines.chunk_content: REM sleep is defined by desynchronized EEG, phasic conjugate eye movements, and profound postural muscle atonia. Evaluate for REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD) if chin EMG demonstrates abnormal motor breakthrough. In patients with severe REM reduction or sleep-onset REM periods (SOREMPs within 15 minutes of sleep onset), conduct structured clinical evaluation for narcolepsy type 1/2 or acute antidepressant discontinuation.

guidelines.document_title: Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnostic Testing for Adult Obstructive Sleep Apnea
guidelines.section_title: Emergency Screening and First-Line Management of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
guidelines.citation_reference: Patil et al., Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 15(2):335-343 (2019/2021)
guidelines.chunk_content: In patients demonstrating recurrent nocturnal micro-arousals accompanied by autonomic surges or repetitive submental EMG tone breaks, initiate comprehensive polysomnography (PSG) evaluation. Recommend continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy as the gold standard for moderate-to-severe OSA. Advise positional therapy (avoiding supine sleep), weight management, and complete avoidance of evening CNS depressants.

guidelines.document_title: APA Stress in Higher Education Standards & NICE CG113
guidelines.section_title: Acute Student Stress & State Anxiety Rapid Intervention
guidelines.chunk_content: For participants exhibiting acute cognitive stress or state anxiety paroxysms: recommend immediate sensory grounding via the 5-4-3-2-1 technique, initiate 4 cycles of 4-7-8 diaphragmatic breathing to stimulate parasympathetic vagal recovery, and enforce structured study hygiene with 25-minute Pomodoro intervals. If symptoms persist beyond transient acute stress, trigger formal referral to university campus mental health counseling.

guidelines.document_title: American Psychological Association (APA) Mind-Body Health Framework
guidelines.chunk_content: Baseline resting physiological state confirmed: participant displays synchronized posterior alpha rhythm and low beta agitation. Advise continued preventive wellness practices including consistent nocturnal circadian sleep patterns, periodic cognitive decompression breaks, hydration, and structured study intervals.

guidelines.document_title: AASM Clinical Practice Guidelines & NICE NG148
guidelines.section_title: Pre-Apnea Airway Stability & Nocturnal Hypoxia Mitigation
guidelines.citation_reference: AASM (Kapur et al. J Clin Sleep Med 13(3):479-504) & NICE NG148
guidelines.chunk_content: Pre-apnea lookback window demonstrates respiratory effort variance and progressive EEG delta slowing indicating imminent upper airway collapse. Recommend immediate positional sleep adjustments (lateral decubitus position, head-of-bed elevation 30 degrees) and comprehensive sleep specialist consultation for diagnostic in-lab Polysomnography (PSG) or Home Sleep Apnea Testing (HSAT).
